rationale: B uses the well-known closed-form approach. It sorts the counts, reads off how many groups of each size the natural layering produces from the differences between adjacent counts, and then makes the one known correction: it turns each (5, 3) pair into two 4s. The code is short and well commented, the reasoning is easy to check, and the result is clearly correct. A uses a greedy loop with an ad hoc heuristic (take a four-group when counts[2] > counts[3]) and re-sorts after every group. That heuristic is harder to reason about and its optimality is not obvious. The loop also repeats long runs of manual decrements in each switch case, and the comment about a 4+2 versus 3+3 trade-off is not actually used. B is clearer, more idiomatic and easier to trust.
